title: Financial concept types overview
summary: Financial concepts classify the operational nature of a movement before the record is posted.
guidance: INCOME is used for incoming resources
OUTGO is used for outgoing payments or expenses
PURCHASE is used when the movement belongs to a purchase flow
REVERSAL is used for reversals or adjustments that undo a prior movement

title: Statement category overview
summary: Statement category defines how the concept is interpreted in the financial statements and business reporting.
guidance: REVENUE covers regular income and period revenue
COGS covers direct costs tied to a specific activity or delivery
OPEX covers recurring operating expenses
CAPEX covers long-term investments and durable asset spending
MINISTRY_TRANSFERS covers transfers to ministries
OTHER covers extraordinary or less routine items

title: Financial concept indicators overview
summary: The concept indicators explain whether a movement affects cash flow, result, patrimonial movement and whether it is operational.
guidance: affectsCashFlow indicates whether available money changes
affectsResult indicates whether the movement should compose the DRE or period result
affectsBalance indicates whether the movement has patrimonial impact beyond pure result interpretation
isOperational indicates whether the movement belongs to ordinary recurring operations

title: Concept meaning versus statement category
summary: Type and statement category are related but different decisions and should not be confused.
guidance: Type answers what kind of movement it is operationally
Statement category answers how the movement should be reported
A good concept should have a reusable name and description, then a coherent statement category and indicators

title: Recurring versus non-recurring concept logic
summary: A concept should reflect whether the movement belongs to ordinary recurring church operation or to a more exceptional case.
guidance: Use recurring operating logic for ordinary, repeated church expenses and revenues
Avoid using a recurring operating concept for a truly exceptional or isolated case
When the case is occasional, let the concept description and indicators reflect that non-recurring nature

title: CAPEX versus OPEX concept logic
summary: Long-term asset acquisition should not be classified the same way as normal recurring operating expense.
guidance: Use OPEX for recurring operational expenses of the period
Use CAPEX when the spending represents a durable investment or long-term church asset
If the purchase creates a church asset that should be tracked, review patrimony follow-up as well

title: Ministry transfer versus other category
summary: Ministry transfer should be used only when the church intentionally treats the movement as a transfer to ministry, not just as any unusual expense.
guidance: Use MINISTRY_TRANSFERS when the configured concept explicitly represents a transfer to ministry
Use OTHER for exceptional items that are not ordinary operations and do not fit a more precise category
Do not default to ministry transfer only because the expense feels special or non-routine

title: Direct cost versus operating expense logic
summary: A cost directly tied to a specific event, delivery or activity should be distinguished from general recurring operating expenses.
guidance: Use COGS when the expense is directly tied to a specific event, conference, retreat or delivery activity
Use OPEX for recurring administrative and operational expenses of the period
Do not default to OPEX when the spending clearly exists because of one identifiable event

title: Benevolence should not be hidden inside generic OPEX
summary: Targeted social aid and benevolence should be represented by a more specific concept than a generic recurring office or administrative expense.
guidance: Prefer a benevolence or assistance concept when the church already configured one
Avoid using a generic administrative OPEX concept for help given to a family or person in need
If no suitable concept exists, review the financial concept catalog before posting
